items.title: 字节发现 DeepSeek 隐藏 Bug，加点空格，模型翻车
items.summary: DeepSeek 的省钱杀手锏，为何成了致命盲区？ 作者丨 高允毅 编辑丨岑 峰 同一个问题问 DeepSeek 两次，只是多敲了几个空格，给出的答案居然一个像“天才”，一个像“智障”。 9月底，字节团队的最新论文 《Periodic Weak Spots: Phase Sensitivity from Chunked KV-Cache Compression》 ，直接点名了 DeepSeek V4 系列模型的 “神鬼二象性 ”问题。 图注：论文链接 https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.36322 这本质上是底层算法偷懒导致的“周期性失忆”， 分块 KV Cache 压缩技术 把长上下文切块压缩处理，这就带来一个问题： “位置决定命运” 。如果你的核心词不巧落在了切块交界的“信息盲区”里，那模型只能胡言乱语。 想象一下，如果让大模型审阅几十页合同，而关键条款刚好卡在“信息盲区”，模型直接无视这条信息，给出相反的结论。而这个错误可能是你不小心加了点空白字符，模型直接翻了车，你还根本不知道问题出在哪。 而这种“神鬼二象性”的先天短板，绝非 DeepSeek 一家独有。在…

items.title: xorbitsai/inference v4.0.0

extra.evidence: # What's new in 4.0.0 (2026-10-10) ## Highlights Xinference 4.0 brings Xavier to more inference engines, enables heterogeneous prefill/decode deployments across engines and hardware, and lets you reconfigure running models without reloading their weights. - **Xavier across vLLM, SGLang, and MLX.** Xavier now supports all three engines, extending prefix KV cache sharing across compatible replicas. Reuse previously computed context across requests and replicas to avoid repeated prefill work. - **Cross-engine and cross-hardware P/D separation.** Run prefill and decode with different inference engines, including vLLM ↔ SGLang and bidirectional NVIDIA ↔ Apple silicon deployments. Choose engines and hardware independently for each role through Xinference’s unified serving interface. - **Reload engines without reloading model weights.** Opt-in GPU weight caching lets vLLM and SGLang retain weights while rebuilding the inference engine. Adjust supported concurrency, context, memory, and CUDA graph settings while preserving the model UID. - **Distributed vLLM V1 inference.** Combine tensor and pipeline parallelism across Xinference workers through the xoscar executor, with improved pipeline scheduling and failure handling. - **One-command installation and service management.** Install and start Xinference on Linux, macOS, and Windows in an isolated Python environment. Optional system services support background operation and automatic startup, with rollback for failed managed service…

items.title: Rethinking Cross-Tokenizer On-Policy Distillation: From Alignment Coverage to Supervision Reliability
items.summary: On-Policy Distillation (OPD) trains a student on its own generations using teacher feedback. With different tokenizers, comparing teacher and student predictions requires alignment at both sequence and vocabulary levels. In this paper, we examine whether expanding this alignment coverage improves learning. Across three heterogeneous teacher--student pairs on mathematical reasoning and code generation, strict 1:1 groups already cover most student-generated tokens despite substantial vocabulary mismatch. items.title: Kandinsky 6.0 Video: Foundation Models for Synchronized Video and Audio Generation
items.summary: We present Kandinsky 6.0 Video, a family of foundation diffusion models for synchronized text-to-audio-video generation, comprising Kandinsky 6.0 Video Lite (3B parameters) and Kandinsky 6.0 Video Pro (29B parameters). Both models generate 5-second video clips with synchronized 44 kHz audio, including lip-sync, in text-to-audio-video (T2AV) and image-to-audio-video (I2AV) modes; a built-in super-resolution model raises the output resolution to Full-HD (1920times1080). items.title: Long-WAM: Scaling the Context of World-Action Models
items.summary: Real-time robot control demands enough visual history to infer motion and task progress, but processing that history can delay action. We present Long-WAM, a model-system framework for scaling the context of causal world-action models under real-time control constraints. Our central finding is that access to history is not the same as using it: longer histories pay off far more when the video foundation is pretrained autoregressively (AR). We first learn causal prediction from robot and egocentric videos without action labels, then preserve this history-to-future structure during world-action…

items.title: Learn2Play Bench: How Well Do LLM Agents Learn from Experience in Unfamiliar Environments?
items.summary: Learning from experience is essential for LLM agents to adapt to unfamiliar and dynmaic environments. Evaluating this ability is therefore important for understanding how effectively agents acquire and use new knowledge. Existing benchmarks have sought to evaluate this ability, but they primarily evaluate tasks whose rules are provided in the instructions or already familiar to pretrained models, making it difficult to distinguish learning from interactions from reasoning with existing knowledge. items.title: nanoMuse: An Open-Source Personal Agent for Every Device You Own
items.summary: Assistants from 2011 answered and waited, and agents from 2023 did a task and stopped. In September 2026 Meta's Muse showed an agent for one person, with accounts, devices, memory and a conversation that lasts, closed, in a vendor's cloud, in one country. Such an agent is expected to act on a person's accounts and devices, remember them across weeks, speak first when it is worth it, and answer for what it did.
